name: Example: Using the Trapezoidal Rule With Irregular Step Size
problem:
Using the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[1,4.5] = [1,2] \cup [2,4] \cup [4,4.5],
$$

approximate the area under the curve of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ whose data is given in the table below.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $4.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $5$ | $7$ | $9$ |
worked_solution:
Let's plot what this function might look like, using the values given in the table.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14055663/assets/975c49f3fc3bed42149ff267cf17455cd816df4297d6909d0c62072ec5688bd2.png)

We've drawn some trapezoids to help calculate our trapezoidal rule sum. By calculating the area of each trapezoid, we obtain the following approximation for our area $\mathcal{A}\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14055663/assets/4caf59c8cb226e10b58407abbff7096cac8113bb0193c58aa200dd4c956722e5.png)

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the above expression gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈\frac{1+5}{2}\cdot (2-1)+\frac{5+7}{2}\cdot (4-2)+\frac{7+9}{2}\cdot (4.5-4) \\  & =3\cdot 1+6\cdot 2+8\cdot 0.5 \\  & =3+12+4 \\  & =19\,.\end{aligned}
$$
